section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that matters accomplished above through Israel's service before the work are not as elevated as after, using the example of G-d's mitzvos which have two aspects: the arousal from above before Israel's service and the superior arousal from above that comes through Israel's service.
section.t: However, nevertheless,
the matters that are done above
(through the service of Israel)
before the service,
are not at the same level of elevation as they are after the service.
And this is analogous to the well-known matter regarding the statement, "He declares His words to Yaakov, His statutes and judgments to Israel."39
[The explanation of "His words, statutes and judgments" is that the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills the mitzvos40],
that there are two aspects to this.41
The first aspect is,
as the Sages, of blessed memory, expounded on the verse, "What He does, He tells Israel to do,"
meaning that initially the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills the mitzvos, and this gives strength to Israel that they should fulfill the mitzvos,
an arousal from above that precedes the arousal from below.
And the second aspect is,
that through Israel fulfilling the mitzvos, it is thereby drawn forth above that the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills the mitzvos,42
an arousal from above that comes through the arousal from below.
And this aspect of the mitzvos of the Holy One, blessed be He, that is brought about through the fulfillment of the mitzvos by Israel,
is more elevated than the fulfillment of the mitzvos of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is in and of itself.43
And this is analogous to the arousal from above that comes through the arousal from below, which is more elevated than the arousal from above that precedes the arousal from below.44

And just as the mitzvos of the Holy One, blessed be He, that are brought about through Israel fulfilling the mitzvos are more elevated than the mitzvos of the Holy One, blessed be He, as they are in and of themselves,
so too can it be said regarding the mitzvos of the Holy One, blessed be He, that are brought about through the fulfillment of the mitzvos by Israel itself,
that the mitzvos of the Holy One, blessed be He, after the fulfillment of the mitzvos by Israel in actual practice,
are more elevated than the mitzvos of the Holy One, blessed be He
(that were brought about through the fulfillment of the mitzvos by Israel)
before the fulfillment of the mitzvos by Israel in actual practice.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the sixth day of Creation depends on the sixth of Sivan when the Torah was given, because the world's existence was conditional on Israel's actual acceptance of the Torah, and this actual acceptance brings about a greater elevation even in the aspect of receiving the Torah as it was in His thought before creation.
section.t: And with this will be understood what the Sages, of blessed memory, said45
on the verse,46
"And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day,"
that the sixth day of the act of Creation
[for the primary matter of the act of Creation is on the sixth day,
the day when Adam was created,
as we say on Rosh HaShanah,47
"This day is the beginning of Your works."48
And so too is it regarding the 19th of Kislev,
the Rosh HaShanah for the Torah of Chassidus and the ways of Chassidus,
that "this day is the beginning of Your works" — the completion of the true intention in the creation of man49]
is dependent on the sixth day of Sivan, on which the Torah was given,50
for the Holy One, blessed be He, stipulated51
with the act of Creation, saying, "If Israel accepts the Torah
(only then)
you will endure," etc.
For from the fact that the verse makes the sixth day of the act of Creation dependent on the sixth day of Sivan,
it is implied
that the fact that the enduring strength of the act of Creation was actualized on the sixth day of Sivan is
(not only because of the doubt that existed in the land, lest they not accept it,52
but rather)
also according to the truth,
as it was revealed before Heaven
(even beforehand)
that Israel would accept the Torah.
[And it should be added,
that since "if Israel accepts the Torah" is a condition for the act of Creation,
therefore
(even when it is known beforehand that the condition will be fulfilled)
the strength of the act is when the condition is fulfilled in actual practice.53]
And even though this matter
(that Israel actually received the Torah)
also existed with Him, blessed be He, from the beginning,
nevertheless, in addition to the fact that this matter is only from the perspective of the Supernal One
(since with Him, blessed be He, the past and future are one),
as opposed to in the world,54
where this matter did not exist,55
and therefore there was no strength for the existence of the world until the sixth day of Sivan,
behold, through Israel actually receiving the Torah in this physical world
(on the sixth of Sivan),
a more elevated elevation was brought about even in the aspect of the receiving of the Torah as it is in His thought, blessed be He, before creation.56

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the purpose of the soul's descent is primarily to effect the refinement and elevation of the sparks in the world (the teshuvah of the world), which is higher than the teshuvah of the soul itself.
section.t: And the matter is,
as explained above
(in the discourse "Mayim Rabim"57)
regarding the elevation that is brought about in the souls specifically through their descent below,
even though before this they were rooted in His Essence, blessed be He, and He consulted with them, etc.,
that when they are in the aspect of consultation, they are in the category of tzaddikim
(as per the precise wording, "Whom did He consult? With the souls of the tzaddikim"58),
and through the service of Torah and mitzvos
(in actual practice)
in their descent below, they become in the level of baalei teshuvah,
the matter of "And the spirit shall return to G-d Who gave it."59
As explained at length in the aforementioned discourse.
And based on the well-known teaching60
that the ultimate intention of the soul's descent below is in order to rectify the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world,
it can be said,
that also the effect in the world
(in the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world,
and even in the entire world)
that is brought about through the service of the soul,
is the matter of teshuvah,
the elevation of all the sparks in the aspect of the returning light of teshuvah.61
And on the contrary,
the ultimate intention of the soul's descent below is
(not for the sake of the elevation of teshuvah that is brought about in the soul,
but rather)
in order to effect the refinement and elevation of the sparks in the world
(the matter of the teshuvah of the world,
and this is higher than the teshuvah of the soul62).
